title: Strain-controlled sign reversal of the anomalous Hall effect in Ru/[Co/Ni]$_N$ multilayers
authors: Jingying Zhang, Sigang Wang, Yue Xiang, Wenhui Xie, Zhe Yuan, Yi Liu, Zongzhi Zhang
abstract: The anomalous Hall effect (AHE) is a hallmark transport phenomenon in ferromagnets arising from relativistic spin-orbit interaction. Here, we report an unexpected sign reversal of the AHE in Ru/[Co/Ni]$_N$ multilayers controlled by the stacking sequence of the Ru layer. When Ru is placed beneath, rather than atop, the Co/Ni multilayers, the anomalous Hall signal switches from positive to negative. By systematically varying the multilayer repeat number N and combining transport measurements with first-principles calculations, we show that this reversal originates from in-plane tensile strain imposed by the Ru underlayer, which reshapes the electronic structure and redistributes Berry curvature near the Fermi level. Our findings establish interfacial strain as an effective knob for tuning Berry-curvature-driven transport and suggest a pathway toward strain-controlled topological transport phenomena in magnetic multilayers.
summary: This research demonstrates that placing a Ruthenium underlayer beneath Co/Ni multilayers can induce a dramatic sign reversal in the Anomalous Hall Effect. This effect is experimentally linked to tensile strain generated by lattice mismatch, which theoretical calculations confirm reshapes the electronic band structure and redistributes Berry curvature, offering a new pathway for strain-controlled topological transport.
main_problem: The study investigates how strain, specifically induced by an underlayer, can control the sign of the Anomalous Hall Effect (AHE) in magnetic multilayers.
main_result: Introducing a Ru underlayer causes a robust sign reversal of the AHE from positive to negative, which is theoretically attributed to tensile in-plane strain reshaping the electronic structure and Berry curvature near the Fermi level.
method: The work combines experimental transport measurements (measuring anomalous Hall resistivity) with first-principles density functional theory (DFT) calculations that incorporate lattice strain effects.
model_or_system: The physical system is $	ext{Ru}/[	ext{Co}/	ext{Ni}]_N$ multilayers, characterized by a strong (111) crystallographic texture and exhibiting perpendicular magnetic anisotropy. The theoretical modeling uses DFT to calculate the anomalous Hall conductivity ($\sigma_{AH}$) under varying strain.
key_observables: Anomalous Hall resistivity ($ho_{AH}$), Anomalous Hall Conductivity ($\sigma_{AH}$), Berry curvature distribution, and lattice strain ($\epsilon$).
important_parameters: Multilayer repeat number ($N$), the presence/position of the Ru layer (underlayer vs. capping layer), and the magnitude of tensile in-plane strain.
main_assumptions: The sign reversal is primarily due to lattice mismatch inducing tensile strain, rather than simple interfacial atomic intermixing or current shunting effects.
figures_summary: Figures show $ho_{AH}$ hysteresis loops demonstrating opposite polarities based on Ru placement. Theoretical figures illustrate the dependence of $\sigma_{AH}$ on strain and map out the sign reversal of Berry curvature contributions in momentum space ($k_z$).
paper_structure: The paper establishes the experimental observation of AHE sign reversal upon placing Ru under the Co/Ni stack, contrasts this with capping layers, and then uses DFT calculations to microscopically prove that tensile strain modifies the electronic bands, leading to a Berry curvature-driven sign change.
why_interesting: While focused on magnetism, the concept of using controlled lattice strain (a structural parameter) to tune topological transport properties like Berry curvature is highly relevant to engineering quantum materials and simulating emergent phenomena in condensed matter theory.

(a) Schematic illustration of the multilayer stack architecture and Hall bar geometry used for electrical transport measurements. (b) XRD patterns of [Co/Ni]N multilayers with a repeat number of 𝑁= 16, showing a pronounced (111) preferential orientation. Out-of-plane and in-plane magnetic hysteresis loops measured for (c) the [Co/Ni]4 and (d) Ru/[Co/Ni]4 samples. The square out-of-plane loops and large in-plane saturation fields confirm robust PMA in both structures. Insets schematically depict the corresponding layer stacking sequences, highlighting the repeated Co/Ni layers and the Ru underlayer.

FIG. 2. Ru-layer-induced reversal of the anomalous Hall effect in Co/Ni multilayers. Room temperature anomalous Hall resistivity (𝜌AH) as a function of out- of-plane magnetic field (𝐻𝑧) for (a) [Co/Ni]4, (b) [Co/Ni]4/Ru, (c) Ru/[Co/Ni]4, and (d) Ru/[Ni/Co]4 samples. While the [Co/Ni]4 and [Co/Ni]4/Ru structures exhibit identical AHE polarity, the insertion of a Ru underlayer leads to a pronounced reversal and suppression of 𝜌AH, independent of whether Co or Ni is in direct contact with Ru. Insets schematically illustrate the corresponding layer stacking sequences, highlighting the Co/Ni multilayers and the position of the Ru layer.

FIG. 3. Thickness-dependent anomalous Hall transport and strain-induced sign reversal. (a) Anomalous Hall resistivity 𝜌AH, (b) longitudinal resistivity 𝜌𝑥𝑥 and (c) AHC 𝜎AH as a function of the Co/Ni repeat number N for [Co/Ni]N and Ru/[Co/Ni]N multilayers. While the Ru-free [Co/Ni]N samples exhibit a largely monotonic evolution of 𝜎AH, the Ru/[Co/Ni]N series displays pronounced nonmonotonic behavior and sign reversals. (d) Calculated 𝜎AH for Co/Ni multilayer as a function of in-plane strain, demonstrating a strain-driven sign change.
